# ANOVA


## [**An**]{style="color:#b04c19"}alysis [**o**]{style="color:#5a55fa"}f [**Va**]{style="color:#dfc127"}riance (**[AN]{style="color:#b04c19"}[O]{style="color:#5a55fa"}[VA]{style="color:#dfc127"}**)

[**An**]{style="color:#b04c19"}alysis [**o**]{style="color:#5a55fa"}f [**Va**]{style="color:#dfc127"}riance (**[AN]{style="color:#b04c19"}[O]{style="color:#5a55fa"}[VA]{style="color:#dfc127"}**)

Method of understanding how categorical variables are related to a continuous outcome of interest

Compares *between groups* to *within groups* variance to jointly compare multiple means


## ANOVA: Partitioning Variance

**Total Sum of Squared Errors:** error term around the grand mean

$$ SS_{total} = \sum (x_i - \bar{x})^2 $$ 

If we have outcomes separated into different groups (e.g., control, treatment A, treatment B), can partition $SS_{total}$ into *between groups sums of squares* $SS_B$ and *within groups sums of squares* $SS_W$

$$ SS_{total} = SS_B + SS_W $$

[So, with $j$ indexing $J$ total groups and $i$ indexing $I$ people within a group, we can write $SS_{total}$ as...]{.fragment}

## ANOVA: Partitioning Variance

**Total Sum of Squared Errors:** error term around the grand mean

$$ SS_{total} = \sum_{j=1}^J \sum_{i=1}^I (x_{ij} - \bar{x})^2 $$ 

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Between-Group Sum of Squares:** error between the group mean and the grand mean

$$ SS_{B} = \sum_{j=1}^J n_j (\bar{x_{j}} - \bar{x})^2 $$ 
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Within-Group Sum of Squares:** error between observations and their group mean

$$ SS_{W} = \sum_{j=1}^J \sum_{i=1}^I (x_{ij} - \bar{x_{j}})^2 $$ 
:::
::::


## ANOVA: Partitioning Variance

Let's say we have three groups and some outcome variable


## ANOVA: Partitioning Variance

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-align: center
n <- 1000
data.frame(i = seq(0, 15, length.out = n)) |>
  mutate(g1 = dnorm(i, 4, 1),
         g2 = dnorm(i, 6, 1),
         g3 = dnorm(i, 11, 1)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = i)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = g1), color = "#b04c19", linewidth = 3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = g2), color = "#5a55fa", linewidth = 3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = g3), color = "#dfc127", linewidth = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 5, 10, 15)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 15), ylim = c(0, .5), expand = F) +
  guides(y = "none", x = guide_axis(cap = "both")) +
  labs(y = NULL, x = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 20)
```


## ANOVA: Partitioning Variance

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-align: center
n <- 20
i <- 100

dat <- data.frame(i = 1:n) |>
  mutate(x1 = rnorm(n, 4, 1),
         x2 = rnorm(n, 6, 1),
         x3 = rnorm(n, 11, 1),
         h_x1 = runif(n, 0, dnorm(x1, 4, 1) * .9),
         h_x2 = runif(n, 0, dnorm(x2, 6, 1) * .9),
         h_x3 = runif(n, 0, dnorm(x3, 11, 1) * .9))

data.frame(i = seq(0, 15, length.out = i)) |>
  mutate(g1 = dnorm(i, 4, 1),
         g2 = dnorm(i, 6, 1),
         g3 = dnorm(i, 11, 1)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = i)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = g1), color = "#b04c19", linewidth = 3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = g2), color = "#5a55fa", linewidth = 3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = g3), color = "#dfc127", linewidth = 3) +
  geom_point(aes(x = x1, y = h_x1), dat, color = "#b04c19") +
  geom_point(aes(x = x2, y = h_x2), dat, color = "#5a55fa") +
  geom_point(aes(x = x3, y = h_x3), dat, color = "#dfc127") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 5, 10, 15)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 15), ylim = c(0, .5), expand = F) +
  guides(y = "none", x = guide_axis(cap = "both")) +
  labs(y = NULL, x = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 20)
```


## ANOVA: Partitioning Variance

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-align: center

data.frame(i = seq(0, 15, length.out = i)) |>
  mutate(g1 = dnorm(i, 4, 1),
         g2 = dnorm(i, 6, 1),
         g3 = dnorm(i, 11, 1)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = i)) +
  annotate("segment", x = mean(c(dat$x1, dat$x2, dat$x3)), y = 0, yend = .45, color = "gray60",
           linewidth = 3, linetype = "dashed") +
  annotate("text", x = mean(c(dat$x1, dat$x2, dat$x3)),
           label = paste("grand mean = ", round(mean(c(dat$x1, dat$x2, dat$x3)), 2)),
           y = Inf, color = "gray60", size = 8, vjust = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(y = g1), color = "#b04c19", linewidth = 3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = g2), color = "#5a55fa", linewidth = 3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = g3), color = "#dfc127", linewidth = 3) +
  geom_point(aes(x = x1, y = h_x1), dat, color = "#b04c19") +
  geom_point(aes(x = x2, y = h_x2), dat, color = "#5a55fa") +
  geom_point(aes(x = x3, y = h_x3), dat, color = "#dfc127") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 5, 10, 15)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 15), ylim = c(0, .5), expand = F) +
  guides(y = "none", x = guide_axis(cap = "both")) +
  labs(y = NULL, x = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 20)
```

## Partitioning Variance: $SS_B$

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-align: center

data.frame(i = seq(0, 15, length.out = i)) |>
  mutate(g1 = dnorm(i, 4, 1),
         g2 = dnorm(i, 6, 1),
         g3 = dnorm(i, 11, 1)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = i)) +
  annotate("segment", x = mean(c(dat$x1, dat$x2, dat$x3)), y = 0, yend = .45, color = "gray60",
           linewidth = 3, linetype = "dashed") +
  annotate("text", x = mean(c(dat$x1, dat$x2, dat$x3)),
           label = paste("grand mean = ", round(mean(c(dat$x1, dat$x2, dat$x3)), 2)),
           y = Inf, color = "gray60", size = 8, vjust = 1) +
  annotate("segment", x = 4, y = 0, yend = dnorm(4, 4, 1), color = "#b04c19",
           linewidth = 2, linetype = "dashed") +
  annotate("text", x = 4, y = dnorm(4, 4, 1),
           label = "group 1 mean", vjust = -1.2,
           color = "#b04c19", size = 8) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = mean(c(x1, x2, x3)), xend = 4, y = dnorm(4, 4, 1)), color = "#b04c19",
               linewidth = 2, data = dat) +
  annotate("segment", x = 6, y = 0, yend = dnorm(6, 6, 1), color = "#5a55fa",
           linewidth = 2, linetype = "dashed") +
  annotate("text", x = 6, y = dnorm(6, 6, 1),
           label = "group 2 mean", vjust = -.4,
           color = "#5a55fa", size = 8) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = mean(c(x1, x2, x3)), xend = 6, y = dnorm(6, 6, 1) - .05), color = "#5a55fa",
               linewidth = 2, data = dat) +
  annotate("segment", x = 11, y = 0, yend = dnorm(11, 11, 1), color = "#dfc127",
           linewidth = 2, linetype = "dashed") +
  annotate("text", x = 11, y = dnorm(11, 11, 1),
           label = "group 3 mean", vjust = -.8,
           color = "#dfc127", size = 8) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = mean(c(x1, x2, x3)), xend = 11, y = dnorm(11, 11, 1) - .025), color = "#dfc127",
               linewidth = 2, data = dat) +
  geom_line(aes(y = g1), color = "#b04c19", linewidth = 3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = g2), color = "#5a55fa", linewidth = 3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = g3), color = "#dfc127", linewidth = 3) +
  geom_point(aes(x = x1, y = h_x1), dat, color = "#b04c19") +
  geom_point(aes(x = x2, y = h_x2), dat, color = "#5a55fa") +
  geom_point(aes(x = x3, y = h_x3), dat, color = "#dfc127") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 5, 10, 15)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 15), ylim = c(0, .5), expand = F) +
  guides(y = "none", x = guide_axis(cap = "both")) +
  labs(y = NULL, x = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 20)
```

```{r}
  geom_line(aes(y = g2), color = "#5a55fa", linewidth = 3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = g3), color = "#dfc127", linewidth = 3) +
  geom_point(aes(x = x1, y = h_x1), dat, color = "#b04c19") +
  geom_point(aes(x = x2, y = h_x2), dat, color = "#5a55fa") +
  geom_point(aes(x = x3, y = h_x3), dat, color = "#dfc127") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 5, 10, 15)) +
```
```{r}
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 15), ylim = c(0, .2), expand = F) +
  guides(y = "none", x = guide_axis(cap = "both")) +
  labs(y = NULL, x = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 20)
```

<!-- ## Partitioning Variance -->

<!-- Ratio of $SS_B$ to $SS_W$ -->

<!-- If $SS_B >> SS_W$, good model. Easy to predict differences based on groups. -->

<!-- If $SS_B \approx SS_W$, less good model. Not easy to predict differences based on groups. -->

<!-- $$ F \propto \frac{\text{between-group variance}}{\text{within-group variance}} $$ -->


## ANOVA: $F$

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Mean Square Between**

$MS_B = \frac{SS_B}{J - 1} = \frac{\sum_{j=1}^J n_j (\bar{x_{j}} - \bar{x})^2}{J - 1}$
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Mean Square Within**

$MS_W = \frac{SS_W}{N - J} = \frac{\sum_{j=1}^J \sum_{i=1}^I (x_{ij} - \bar{x})^2}{N - J}$
:::
::::

<br>

$$ F = \frac{MS_B}{MS_W} $$


## ANOVA: Hypotheses

$H_0$: $\mu_1 = \mu_2 = ... = \mu_J$

$H_1$: not $H_0$

::: fragment
Equivalent to:

$H_0$: $\sigma^2_B = 0$

$H_1$: $\sigma^2_B \neq 0$
:::

## Missing Some Penguins (Data)!

::: {style="font-size:85%"}
The `penguins` dataset has missing data, as do many real-life datasets. `R` represents these as `NA`s.

This is something to definitively be aware of. While many functions will handle missing data in some way for you, which can be convenient, they often do so *silently* (without saying anything!). 

Some functions will simply return `NA`, and these often have an `na.rm` (remove `NA`s) argument. For example,

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="33%"}
```{r}
mean(penguins$flipper_length_mm)
mean(penguins$flipper_length_mm, na.rm = T)
```

:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
```{r}
sd(penguins$flipper_length_mm)
sd(penguins$flipper_length_mm, na.rm = T)
```

:::

::: {.column width="33%"}
```{r}
sum(penguins$flipper_length_mm) /
  length(penguins$flipper_length_mm)

sum(penguins$flipper_length_mm, na.rm = T) /
  length(penguins$flipper_length_mm)
```
:::
::::

:::


## Missing Some Penguins (Data)!

Let's be proactive and remove the missing values ourselves. 

```{r}
penguins_cleaned <- penguins |>
  filter_out(when_any(is.na(flipper_length_mm), is.na(species)))
nrow(penguins); nrow(penguins_cleaned)
```

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
mean(penguins_cleaned$flipper_length_mm)
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
sum(penguins_cleaned$flipper_length_mm) /
  length(penguins_cleaned$flipper_length_mm)
```
:::
::::



# Frequentist ANOVA


## ANOVA: R function

`aov(y ~ grouping_var, data = data)`

::: subpoint
○ `y` = outcome
:::

::: subpoint
○ `grouping_var` = name of grouping variable
:::

::: subpoint
○ `data` = dataframe that includes `grouping_var` and `y`
:::

Very similar syntax to `lm(y ~ predictor, data = data)`

Uses dummy coding by default

`summary(model)` prints out results


## ANOVA: Example

::: fragment
```{r}
flipper_model <- aov(flipper_length_mm ~ species, data = penguins_cleaned)
summary(flipper_model)
```
:::

[Huge $F$-statistic!]{.fragment}

[We reject the null in favor of the alternative that there is significant variation between penguin species in flipper length]{.fragment}


## Effect Sizes: Example

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column .fragment width="50%"}
$\eta^2$

$\frac{SS_B}{SS_T} = \frac{SS_B}{SS_B \ + \ SS_W}$

::: fragment
```{r}
effectsize::eta_squared(flipper_model)
effectsize::eta_squared(flipper_model)$Eta2
```
:::
:::

::: {.column .fragment width="50%"}
$\omega^2$

$\frac{SS_B \ - \ (J - 1)MS_w}{SS_T \ + \ MS_W}$

::: fragment
```{r}
effectsize::omega_squared(flipper_model)
effectsize::omega_squared(flipper_model)$Omega2
```
:::
:::
::::

[In this case, $\eta^2$ and $\omega^2$ happen to be very close. Represent the proportion of variance in flipper length accounted for by differences in species.]{.fragment}

# ANOVA as a Linear Model

## ANOVA as a Linear Model

Like *t*-tests, ANOVAs are just another phrasing of a linear model.

Now, we have a slope term for each of our groups minus one ($J - 1$ for $J$ groups)

::: subpoint
○ Depending on the variable *coding*, the parameters present the information differently.

○ But ultimately, conducting an ANOVA explicitly as a linear model provides all the same information as conducting it in the sums of squares framework.
:::

We are still interested in differences between means of groups, we just have more groups now (compared to *t*-test).

Let's consider an example of an experiment where we have three groups: a control group, a treatment A group, and a treatment B group.


## ANOVA as a Linear Model

::: {style="font-size:90%"}

With **dummy coding**, we use one group as a reference group and compare all others to it by using indicator variables representing belonging in each other group.

$$y = \beta_0 + \beta_A \text{trt}_A + \beta_B \text{trt}_B + \epsilon$$

where $\text{trt}_A = 1$ if the participant was in treatment A and is $0$ otherwise (and similarly for $\text{trt}_B$) 

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Slope Interpretations**

::: subpoint
○ $\beta_0 =$ mean of control group
:::

::: subpoint
○ $\beta_A =$ difference in means between control group and treatment A group
:::

::: subpoint
○ $\beta_B =$ difference in means between control group and treatment B group
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Accessing Group Means**

::: subpoint
○ $\beta_0 =$ mean of control group
:::

::: subpoint
○ $\beta_0 + \beta_A =$ mean of treatment A group
:::

::: subpoint
○ $\beta_0 + \beta_B =$ mean of treatment B group
:::

:::
::::

:::


## ANOVA as a Linear Model

::: {style="font-size:90%"}

With **dummy coding**, we use one group as a reference group and compare all others to it by using indicator variables representing belonging in each other group.

$$y = \beta_0 + \beta_A \text{trt}_A + \beta_B \text{trt}_B + \epsilon$$

where $\text{trt}_A = 1$ if the participant was in treatment A and is $0$ otherwise (and similarly for $\text{trt}_B$) 
:::

```{r}
#| echo: false
set.seed(2026)
n   <- 40
z0  <- as.numeric(scale(rnorm(n)))
zA  <- as.numeric(scale(rnorm(n)))
zB  <- as.numeric(scale(rnorm(n)))

b0 <- 5

make_dummy_plot <- function(bA, bB, title) {
  
  grp <- c("control", "trtA", "trtB")
  df <- tibble(
    group = factor(rep(grp, each = n), levels = grp),
    y     = c(b0 + z0, b0 + bA + zA, b0 + bB + zB)
  )
  
  mA   <- b0 + bA
  mB   <- b0 + bB
  grey <- "grey25"
  arr  <- arrow(length = unit(0.09, "inches"), type = "closed")
  
  bracket <- tibble(
    x    = c(2.45, 3.45),
    ymin = c(min(b0, mA), min(b0, mB)),
    ymax = c(max(b0, mA), max(b0, mB))
  )
  
  ggplot(df, aes(x = group, y = y, fill = group, color = group)) +
    geom_violin(alpha = 0.3, color = NA, width = 0.7) +
    geom_jitter(alpha = 0.6, shape = 16, size = 1.8, width = 0.1, height = 0) +
    
    # Reference line at the control mean, extended across to the brackets
    annotate("segment", x = 1, xend = 3.45, y = b0, yend = b0,
             linetype = "dashed", color = grey, linewidth = 0.4) +
    
    # Group means
    stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", color = "black", size = 3) +
    
    # beta_0: curved arrow + text pointing at the control mean
    annotate("curve", x = 0.62, xend = 0.93, y = b0 + 1.8, yend = b0 + 0.2,
             curvature = 0.35, arrow = arr, color = grey, linewidth = 0.5) +
    annotate("text", x = 0.58, y = b0 + 2.2, label = "beta[0]",
             parse = TRUE, color = grey, size = 4.5) +
    
    # beta_A and beta_B: errorbar-style brackets spanning each difference from control
    geom_errorbar(data = bracket, aes(x = x, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax),
                  width = 0.08, color = grey, linewidth = 0.6,
                  inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    annotate("text", x = 2.52, y = (b0 + mA) / 2, label = "beta[A]",
             parse = TRUE, hjust = 0, color = grey, size = 4.5) +
    annotate("text", x = 3.52, y = (b0 + mB) / 2, label = "beta[B]",
             parse = TRUE, hjust = 0, color = grey, size = 4.5) +
    
    scale_x_discrete(NULL, labels = expression(
      atop("Control", beta[0]),
      atop("Treatment A", beta[0] + beta[A]),
      atop("Treatment B", beta[0] + beta[B])
    )) +
    scale_y_continuous("Outcome", breaks = seq(2, 10, 2)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("control" = "#7FA6C9",
                                 "trtA"    = "#E8A07A",
                                 "trtB"    = "#8FB8A8")) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("control" = "#3F6E94",
                                  "trtA"    = "#C2623A",
                                  "trtB"    = "#5E8F7D")) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.45, 3.85), ylim = c(0.5, 10.5)) +
    guides(x = guide_axis(cap = TRUE),
           y = guide_axis(cap = TRUE),
           fill = "none", color = "none") +
    labs(title = title) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(axis.line.x = element_blank(),
          axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 10, color = "black"),
          plot.title   = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 11))
}
```

```{r}
#| layout-ncol: 2
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 3
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
make_dummy_plot(bA = 1.5, bB = 3,  "Both treatments higher")
make_dummy_plot(bA = 2,   bB = -2, "A higher, B lower")
```


## ANOVA as a Linear Model

::: {style="font-size:90%"}

With **effect coding**, we let the grand mean be the "reference" point and examine $J - 1$ groups as by their deviation from the grand mean.

$$y = \beta_0 + \beta_A x_A + \beta_B x_B + \epsilon$$

where $x_A = 1$ if the participant was in treatment A, $x_A = -1$ if the participant was in the control, and is $0$ otherwise. Similarly, $x_B = 1$ if the participant was in treatment B, $x_B = -1$ if the participant was in the control, and is $0$ otherwise.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Slope Interpretations**

::: subpoint
○ $\beta_0 =$ overall grand mean
:::

::: subpoint
○ $\beta_A =$ deviation of treatment A from grand mean
:::

::: subpoint
○ $\beta_B =$ deviation of treatment B from grand mean
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Accessing Group Means**

::: subpoint
○ $\beta_0 =$ overall grand mean
:::

::: subpoint
○ $\beta_0 + \beta_A =$ mean of treatment A group
:::

::: subpoint
○ $\beta_0 + \beta_B =$ mean of treatment B group
:::

::: subpoint
○ $\beta_0 + (-1)\beta_A + (-1)\beta_B =$ mean of control group
:::

:::
::::

:::


## ANOVA as a Linear Model

::: {style="font-size:90%"}

With **effect coding**, we let the grand mean be the "reference" point and examine $J - 2$ groups by their deviation from the grand mean.

$$y = \beta_0 + \beta_A x_A + \beta_B x_B + \epsilon$$

where $x_A = 1$ if the participant was in treatment A, $x_A = -1$ if the participant was in the control, and is $0$ otherwise. Similarly, $x_B = 1$ if the participant was in treatment B, $x_B = -1$ if the participant was in the control, and is $0$ otherwise.

:::

```{r}
#| echo: false
set.seed(2026)
n   <- 40
z0  <- as.numeric(scale(rnorm(n)))
zA  <- as.numeric(scale(rnorm(n)))
zB  <- as.numeric(scale(rnorm(n)))

b0 <- 5  # grand mean

make_effect_plot <- function(bA, bB, title) {
  
  bC <- -(bA + bB)   # control's deviation: effects sum to zero
  
  grp <- c("control", "trtA", "trtB")
  df <- tibble(
    group = factor(rep(grp, each = n), levels = grp),
    y     = c(b0 + bC + z0, b0 + bA + zA, b0 + bB + zB)
  )
  
  grey <- "grey25"
  
  bracket <- tibble(
    x    = c(0.6, 2.45, 3.45),
    ymin = b0 + pmin(0, c(bC, bA, bB)),
    ymax = b0 + pmax(0, c(bC, bA, bB))
  )
  
  ggplot(df, aes(x = group, y = y, fill = group, color = group)) +
    geom_violin(alpha = 0.3, color = NA, width = 0.7) +
    geom_jitter(alpha = 0.6, shape = 16, size = 1.8, width = 0.1, height = 0) +
    
    # Grand mean reference line
    annotate("segment", x = 0.6, xend = 3.85, y = b0, yend = b0,
             linetype = "dashed", color = grey, linewidth = 0.4) +
    annotate("text", x = 3.9, y = b0, label = "beta[0]",
             parse = TRUE, hjust = 0, color = grey, size = 4.5) +
    
    # Group means
    stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", color = "black", size = 3) +
    
    # Brackets: deviation of each group from the grand mean
    geom_errorbar(data = bracket, aes(x = x, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax),
                  width = 0.08, color = grey, linewidth = 0.6,
                  inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    annotate("text", x = 0.54, y = b0 + bC / 2, label = "-(beta[A]+beta[B])",
             parse = TRUE, hjust = 1, color = grey, size = 4) +
    annotate("text", x = 2.52, y = b0 + bA / 2, label = "beta[A]",
             parse = TRUE, hjust = 0, color = grey, size = 4.5) +
    annotate("text", x = 3.52, y = b0 + bB / 2, label = "beta[B]",
             parse = TRUE, hjust = 0, color = grey, size = 4.5) +
    
    scale_x_discrete(NULL, labels = expression(
      atop("Control", beta[0] - beta[A] - beta[B]),
      atop("Treatment A", beta[0] + beta[A]),
      atop("Treatment B", beta[0] + beta[B])
    )) +
    scale_y_continuous("Outcome", breaks = seq(2, 8, 2)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("control" = "#7FA6C9",
                                 "trtA"    = "#E8A07A",
                                 "trtB"    = "#8FB8A8")) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("control" = "#3F6E94",
                                  "trtA"    = "#C2623A",
                                  "trtB"    = "#5E8F7D")) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-0.2, 4.25), ylim = c(0, 10)) +
    guides(x = guide_axis(cap = TRUE),
           y = guide_axis(cap = TRUE),
           fill = "none", color = "none") +
    labs(title = title) +
    theme_classic() +
    theme(axis.line.x = element_blank(),
          axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 10, color = "black"),
          plot.title   = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 11))
}
```

```{r}
#| layout-ncol: 2
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 3
#| echo: false
#| fig-align: center
make_effect_plot(bA = 1.75, bB = -1, "A above, B below grand mean")
make_effect_plot(bA = 2,   bB = 1,    "Both treatments above, control far below")
```


## ANOVA as a Linear Model in R

We can conduct ANOVAs explicitly as linear models with `lm(outcome ~ grouping_variable, data = data)`. 

:::: {.columns .fragment}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
flipper_model_lm <- lm(flipper_length_mm ~ species, 
                       data = penguins_cleaned)
summary(flipper_model_lm)
```
:::

::: {.column style="font-size:80%" width="50%"}
With dummy coding, 

::: subpoint
○ `(Intercept)` = mean of reference group (here, $\mu_\text{Adelie}$)
:::

::: subpoint
○ `speciesChinstrap` = difference between target group and reference group (here, $\mu_\text{Chinstrap} - \mu_\text{Adelie}$)
:::

::: subpoint
○ `speciesGentoo` = difference between target group and reference group (here, $\mu_\text{Gentoo} - \mu_\text{Adelie}$)
:::
:::
::::


## Changing to Effect Coding

We can tell `R` we want to use effect coding instead of dummy coding; we don't have to manually create the effect coding columns ourselves.

We need to set the `contrasts` setting of our grouping variable to `contr.sum`. Everything you run after that will use effect coding.

::: fragment
:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Before (default)**
```{r}
contrasts(penguins_cleaned$species)
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**After**

```{r}
contrasts(penguins_cleaned$species) <- contr.sum
contrasts(penguins_cleaned$species)
```
:::
::::

```{r}
flipper_model_lm_effect <- lm(flipper_length_mm ~ species, data = penguins_cleaned)
```
:::

[What two effects will we see in the slope parameters?]{.fragment} [Adelie and Chinstrap!]{.fragment}


## Changing to Effect Coding

We can tell `R` we want to use effect coding instead of dummy coding; we don't have to manually create the effect coding columns ourselves.

We need to set the `contrasts` setting of our grouping variable to `contr.sum`. Everything you run after that will use effect coding.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
summary(flipper_model_lm)
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
summary(flipper_model_lm_effect)
```
:::
::::


## Changing to Effect Coding

By default, `R` switches the *last* level to be the one omitted from the slope paramters. To change, reorder the levels.

```{r}
penguins_cleaned$species_reordered <- factor(penguins_cleaned$species, levels = c("Chinstrap", "Gentoo", "Adelie"))
contrasts(penguins_cleaned$species_reordered) <- contr.sum
contrasts(penguins_cleaned$species_reordered)
```


## Changing to Dummy Coding

Dummy coding is the default, but if you change it to effect coding and need to change it back to dummy coding, set it to `contr.treatment`.

```{r}
contrasts(penguins_cleaned$species) <- contr.treatment # back to dummy coding
contrasts(penguins_cleaned$species)
```



# Bayesian ANOVA

## Bayesian ANOVA: Example

Can use `stan_glm()` within `{rstanarm}` and formula syntax again.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
#| eval: false
library(rstanarm)
flipper_model_bayes <- stan_glm(
  flipper_length_mm ~ species, 
  data = penguins_cleaned, 
  family = "gaussian"
) 
summary(flipper_model_bayes)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
library(rstanarm)
flipper_model_bayes <- stan_glm(
  flipper_length_mm ~ species, 
  data = penguins_cleaned, 
  family = "gaussian",
  refresh = 0
) 
summary(flipper_model_bayes)
```
:::

::: {.column style="font-size:80%" width="50%"}
With dummy coding, 

::: subpoint
○ `(Intercept)` = mean of reference group (here, $\mu_\text{Adelie}$)
:::

::: subpoint
○ `speciesChinstrap` = difference between target group and reference group (here, $\mu_\text{Chinstrap} - \mu_\text{Adelie}$)
:::

::: subpoint
○ `speciesGentoo` = difference between target group and reference group (here, $\mu_\text{Gentoo} - \mu_\text{Adelie}$)
:::

[Not shown here, but changing to effect coding with the same code as before works for `stan_glm()` too.]{.fragment}
:::
::::


## Check Diagnostics

```{r}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 2
summary(flipper_model_bayes) |> as_tibble(rownames = "parameters")
bayesplot::mcmc_trace(flipper_model_bayes, facet_args = list(nrow = 1)) # to show all on one row
```


## What Priors Were Used?

```{r}
prior_summary(flipper_model_bayes)
```


## Visualizing Results

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
Plotting the *posterior predictive distribution* with the original data asks:

How well does our observed data ($y$) compare to the fitted model's predictions ($y_{rep}$)?
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.panel-tabset}
### Plot
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-align: center
bayesplot::ppc_violin_grouped(
  y = penguins_cleaned$flipper_length_mm,
  yrep = posterior_predict(flipper_model_bayes, draws = 50),
  group = penguins_cleaned$species
) 
```

### Code
```{r}
#| eval: false
bayesplot::ppc_violin_grouped(
  y = penguins_cleaned$flipper_length_mm,
  yrep = posterior_predict(flipper_model_bayes, draws = 50),
  group = penguins_cleaned$species
) 
```
:::
:::
::::

<!-- ## Effect Coding -->

<!-- :::: {.columns} -->
<!-- ::: {.column width="50%"} -->
<!-- Dummy coding compares $g-1$ groups to $\beta_0 =$ **reference group mean**: -->

<!-- | Predictor | $g_1$ | $g_2$ | $\cdots$ | $g_{G-1}$ | $g_G$ | -->
<!-- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | -->
<!-- | $x_1$ | 1 | 0 | $\cdots$ | 0 | 0 | -->
<!-- | $x_2$ | 0 | 1 | $\cdots$ | 0 | 0 | -->
<!-- | $\vdots$ | $\vdots$ | $\vdots$ | $\ddots$ | $\vdots$ | $\vdots$ | -->
<!-- | $x_{G-1}$ | 0 | 0 | $\cdots$ | 1 | 0 | -->
<!-- ::: -->

<!-- ::: {.column width="50%"} -->
<!-- **Dummy coding:** -->

<!-- - $\beta_0: = \mu_3$ -->
<!-- - $\beta_1: = \mu_{1} - \mu_3$ -->
<!-- - $\beta_2: = \mu_{2} - \mu_3$ -->
<!-- ::: -->
<!-- :::: -->

<!-- :::: {.columns} -->
<!-- ::: {.column width="50%"} -->
<!-- Effects or contrast coding compares $g-1$ groups to $\beta_0 =$ **grand mean**: -->

<!-- | Predictor | $g_1$ | $g_2$ | $\cdots$ | $g_{G-1}$ | $g_G$ | -->
<!-- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | -->
<!-- | $x_1$ | 1 | 0 | $\cdots$ | 0 | -1 | -->
<!-- | $x_2$ | 0 | 1 | $\cdots$ | 0 | -1 | -->
<!-- | $\vdots$ | $\vdots$ | $\vdots$ | $\ddots$ | $\vdots$ | $\vdots$ | -->
<!-- | $x_{G-1}$ | 0 | 0 | $\cdots$ | 1 | -1 | -->
<!-- ::: -->

<!-- ::: {.column width="50%"} -->
<!-- **Contrast/Effects coding:** -->

<!-- - $\beta_0: = \mu$ -->
<!-- - $\beta_1: = \mu_{1} - \mu$ -->
<!-- - $\beta_2: = \mu_{2} - \mu$ -->

<!-- Compares groups to **grand mean** -->
<!-- ::: -->
<!-- :::: -->
